votes.reasoning: SafeNumeric.swift:22-40 is correct. init(saturating:) returns 0 for NaN and compares with '>= Double(max)', which handles Double(Int64.max) rounding up to 2^63. init?(checkedTruncating:) is exactly(rounded(.towardZero)), which gives nil for NaN, infinity and out-of-range values. JWT.swift:53-54 now returns nil for such a claim. AnthropicCredentials.swift:47,78 saturates. Reversal: jwt_huge_int_claim_is_nil, jwt_huge_int64_claim_is_nil, anthropic_credentials_huge_expiry_saturates and anthropic_rotated_huge_expiry_saturates all crash when reverted. The SafeNumeric unit tests cover the boundaries, including the unsigned and narrow-negative cases. A saturated expiry of Int64.max makes an absurd token look not expired, but as the comment says, the server still rejects it. It is also only a local comparison, so it does not change authz.

This adds the missing project-wide helper, Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Util/SafeNumeric.swift, 60 lines with two initializers on FixedWidthInteger. It is generic but has real consumers of both forms: saturating for display and ordering, checkedTruncating for decoded fields. The policy is written in the header comment, and the >= boundary is justified, not decorative. The new file has its own @Test suite, as CLAUDE.md §4 requires, covering NaN, ±inf, 2^63, narrow types and unsigned. JWT.swift:52-54 and AnthropicCredentials.swift:45,77 each pick the form that fits their meaning (claim reads as absent vs expiry saturates). CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md are updated in the same turn, following the always-update-docs rule.

The finding is literally 'no project-wide checked Double->Int conversion', so the new public extension in SafeNumeric.swift, the CLAUDE.md hard rule and the identical AGENTS.md text are the fix itself, not scope creep. SafeNumericTests covers the new file. JWT.swift:52-54 now returns nil for claims that cannot be represented, which matches its existing optional contract. AnthropicCredentials.swift:45,77 saturates. It stays Codable-compatible and decodes a Double expiry that would previously have trapped.
